prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
**Block sort** (also called an in-place stable merge sort) fits those requirements:

- **Best case:** \(O(n)\)
- **Average/worst case:** \(O(n\log n)\)
- **Stable:** Yes
- **In-place:** Yes, using \(O(1)\) auxiliary space

Timsort has the same best and worst time bounds but is generally **not in-place**, as it requires additional memory.
